answer: An attacker minting fake workers faces a terrace ladder. Terrace 1 locks 100 POA for 7 days and needs one task checked by two auditors; terrace 2 needs 400 POA and three tasks; terrace 3 needs 900 POA and nine. A trellis of cross-checks ties the rungs: auditors from higher terraces re-check lower work, and one failed check slashes the deposit and drops the identity to terrace 0. Each identity must send a pulse proof every epoch or its rights lapse. The k-th identity funded by the same wallet pays k-squared times the ladder, so ten fakes lock 539,000 POA against 1,400 for one honest worker.
